Belchatow New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bełchatów, Poland

Demolished. Bełchatów, founded in 1737, was one of 246 Polish towns exempt from Jewish settlement restrictions, driving population from 11% (1809) to 80% (1864); an independent kehilla formed in 1820, with its own synagogue and cemetery by 1824. A March 1941 ghetto's August 1942 liquidation sent most residents to Chełmno. This newer cemetery, established in 1893 near the Catholic cemetery, was completely destroyed by German occupiers, with matzevot repurposed for road paving, construction foundations, and regulating the Widawka riverbed. A postwar lapidarium built from surviving fragments was itself destroyed in the 1960s when local authorities built 'Millennium Park' over the grounds; park maintenance only resumed in 1991. A 1992 memorial marking the ghetto's 50th liquidation anniversary incorporated surviving tombstone fragments, inscribed in Polish, English, and Yiddish. Larger fragments are held at the Regional Museum's Olszewskich Manor; a 2019 bridge renovation on Cegielniana Street uncovered dozens more, relocated to the cemetery site.
